calendar_note: Every date in this record is synthetic and belongs to the hypothetical Project Northcell. No organisation, plant, vehicle, technician or recycler named here exists.
purpose: State what may and may not be done to the item by whom, in what order, and with what safety warning. The safety property this record protects is not the item's; it is the technician's, because a procedure that can be misperformed on a 400 volt pack injures the person following it.

in_scope: Component replacement and the recalibration it requires
Reading the item's record before acting on it
Return to service after any action
out_of_scope: Pack-level work and pack-level safety, which the pack integrator owns
Any action on a pack that a qualified technician should not perform alone, which this procedure does not authorise at all
Instructions for a vehicle owner, which would be a separate document written for a non-technical reader

responsible_roles.responsibility: Owns this record and its revision
May perform the procedures below and only those marked as within their training

responsible_roles.named_as: role identity: safety_engineer (safety warning approver, fictional)
responsible_roles.responsibility: Approves the safety warnings and their wording

responsible_roles.named_as: role identity: sw_engineer (software action owner, fictional)
responsible_roles.responsibility: Owns the reprogramming and the parameter restoration after replacement

procedures.action: Before any work: confirm the item's configuration identification and retrieve the non-volatile event log
procedures.acceptance_condition: The identification is read and recorded, and the log is captured before anything that could overwrite it
procedures.decision_point: Whether work may proceed without a readable identification, which this procedure forbids

procedures.action: Confirm the vehicle is in the state the procedure requires, with the high-voltage system isolated by the vehicle's own means
procedures.acceptance_condition: Isolation is confirmed by the vehicle, not by this item; the item may only observe it and may not be asked to provide it

procedures.action: Perform the action in the order given for the procedure selected, without skipping a step
procedures.acceptance_condition: Every step in the selected procedure was performed in the given order
procedures.decision_point: Whether a step that cannot be performed may be skipped, which this procedure forbids

procedures.action: After any component replacement, restore the affected parameter values from the calibration specification rather than from memory or from another item
procedures.acceptance_condition: Every affected parameter resolves to its canonical parameter id and value, and the item passes the post-service check
procedures.decision_point: Whether an item may be returned to service with a parameter restored from an unverified source, which this procedure forbids

procedures.action: Perform the post-service check: confirm the item reaches and confirms the safe state on a fault injection, and confirm the configuration identification still resolves
procedures.acceptance_condition: The safe state is reached within the fault-tolerant time interval and the identification resolves to exactly one configuration

procedures.action: Return the item to service only with the post-service record complete and the event log archived
procedures.acceptance_condition: No item returns to service with an incomplete post-service record
procedures.decision_point: Whether a return to service may proceed with a degraded post-service check, which this procedure forbids

records_produced.identification_rule: Vehicle identification, configuration identification and read date
Replaced component plus each restored parameter id and value
Post-service check result and the configuration identification

acceptance_criteria.measure: Service events where the log was captured before any overwriting action
Restored parameter values resolved from the calibration specification
Post-service checks reaching the safe state within the interval
Procedures performed without a skipped step
Service actions performed by a role not marked as permitted for that procedure

service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: A commissioning technician trained on this procedure. In this corpus that role is fictional and no training exists.
steps: Confirm the item is not fitted in a pack or is fitted with all cables disconnected
Connect the service supply and confirm the supply indication
Connect the sense leads one module at a time, confirming the cell count after each
Assert commissioning and confirm that contactor actuation is inhibited
Read the configuration identification and confirm it resolves to the configuration this item should carry
Release commissioning, remove the service tool and confirm the item is inert
service_procedures.safety_warning: A new item with unconnected sense leads will report those inputs as out of range if commissioning is asserted incorrectly. Do not attempt to command the contactors closed at any point in this procedure. If the item does not behave as described, stop and escalate rather than continuing.

service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: A service technician trained on this procedure
steps: Capture the event log before disconnecting anything
Isolate the high-voltage system by the vehicle's own means and confirm it
Disconnect the slave and replace it
Recalibrate the affected sensor tables against a reference measurement
Verify the cell count and the values against the pack's build record
Perform the post-service check
service_procedures.safety_warning: A replaced slave runs on the previous slave's calibration table until it is recalibrated. Do not return the vehicle to service between replacement and recalibration: in that interval the item reports cell values it has not measured.

service_procedures.procedure_name: Read and clear a latched fault
service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: A service technician trained on this procedure
steps: Capture the event log
Record every active diagnosis entry and its severity before clearing any
Determine whether the condition that raised the entry is still present
Clear the entry only if the condition is absent
Perform the post-service check
service_procedures.safety_warning: Clearing a latched fault without removing its cause returns the vehicle to service with the condition intact. The item will latch again, but the vehicle may have been driven in between.

service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: A service technician trained on this procedure and authorised for reprogramming
steps: Capture the event log and record the current configuration identification
Confirm the replacement image is the released build and not a development image
Reprogram and verify by readback
Restore every parameter value from the calibration specification
Perform the post-service check and confirm the configuration identification still resolves
service_procedures.safety_warning: Reprogramming without restoring the parameter values leaves the item on whatever values were previously in memory, which may belong to a different pack. Read the parameter values back and compare them against the specification before returning to service.
tools_required: Commissioning tool with the released identity

service_procedures.who_may_perform_it: Any technician who has completed one of SVC-01 to SVC-04
steps: Confirm the item's state and that no safety-severity entry is active other than the one being worked
Inject a fault through the service interface and confirm the item reaches and confirms the safe state within the fault-tolerant time interval
Confirm the configuration identification resolves to exactly one released configuration
Record the result
service_procedures.safety_warning: The fault injection is performed through the service interface and the vehicle must be stationary with the high-voltage system isolated. Do not perform this check with the vehicle in motion or with the pack energised.
service_procedures.post_service_check: None; this procedure is the post-service check

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The technician reads the configuration identification to determine what is fitted
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: A service action is performed against a configuration the technician did not know was fitted, and the action may be inapplicable to it.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: SVC-02 and SVC-04 restore parameters from the calibration specification this area produces
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: A replaced component runs on a stale table and the item reports values it has not measured.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The technician captures the event log before acting
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: The log is overwritten before it is read and the field signal for that vehicle is lost permanently.

interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.interaction: The event log and the configuration identification inform the end-of-life decision
interactions_with_other_lifecycle_areas.consequence_if_the_interaction_is_broken: A pack is retired without the record that would say whether it should have been retired earlier.

operational_authorisation_statement: This record is a fictional engineering artefact. It is NOT an authorised service instruction, it authorises no work on any real equipment, and no technician has performed any procedure in it. It is held at lifecycle_status draft rather than baselined precisely because a service instruction is the record most likely to be acted on. production_authorized is false.

evidence_state.reason: No production line, vehicle, charging site, workshop, fleet or recycling facility exists anywhere in this corpus. Master-prompt clause 2.5 forbids energising hardware and connecting to vehicles, so no step below can be performed by any means available here. The record documents the procedure and records that it has not been run.

limitations: Synthetic. No technician exists, no vehicle exists and no equipment exists. Every procedure below describes work that has not been done.

The safety warnings are engineering statements about the hypothetical item's failure behaviour. They have not been reviewed by a person who has performed the work, which is the review that matters for a service instruction.
The record is held at draft rather than baselined for the reason above. A baselined service instruction in a corpus like this one is an invitation.

SVC-05's fault injection exercises one reaction path on the service interface. It does not exercise the independent hardware path, so an item whose main path is defective could pass this check. The end-of-line plan requires the independent path to be exercised separately; this procedure does not.
The technician named in 'who_may_perform_it' is a fictional role identity. No training record exists for it, and the corpus contains no competence records at all.

Nothing in this procedure is derived from an existing manufacturer document. The real foxBMS project publishes developer documentation, not a service instruction, and no part of this record is presented as one.
